Journal Management System

Official User Manual & Workflow Documentation

1. Introduction & General System Workflow

The Journal Management System is a comprehensive digital platform designed to handle the entire lifecycle of academic publishing. From the moment a manuscript is submitted, through the rigorous peer-review process, and all the way to final publication, this system tracks every step to ensure transparency and efficiency.

This guide provides step-by-step instructions for all users interacting with the system.

Understanding the User Roles

The system operates using four distinct user roles, ensuring that everyone only sees the tools and information necessary for their specific tasks:

  1. Authors: Individuals submitting their original research for publication. Authors have the ability to upload their manuscripts, track the real-time status of their submissions, read feedback provided by reviewers, and upload revised versions of their work when requested.
  2. Reviewers: Subject-matter experts invited to evaluate submissions. Reviewers receive email invitations which they can accept or decline. Once accepted, they gain access to the manuscript and can submit a structured assessment, detailing both public feedback for the author and private recommendations for the editorial team.
  3. Editors: The managers overseeing the peer-review process. Editors are responsible for screening new submissions, assigning peer reviewers to manuscripts, monitoring the progress of those reviews, and ultimately deciding the fate of the manuscript (such as accepting it, rejecting it, or requesting revisions).
  4. Administrators (Superadmins): The overseers of the entire platform. Administrators possess all the capabilities of an Editor, alongside high-level controls such as creating new Volumes and Issues, publishing accepted manuscripts to the live website, and managing staff accounts.

[!NOTE] It is entirely possible for a single user account to hold multiple roles simultaneously. For example, a registered Author can also be invited by an Editor to act as a Reviewer for a different manuscript.

The Big Picture: System Workflow

Every manuscript processed by the system follows a strict, structured lifecycle organized into "Rounds." This ensures that documents can be reviewed, revised, and re-reviewed multiple times if necessary without losing historical data.

Here is a visual representation mapping how a document moves through the various stages of the system:

The Workflow Explained Step-by-Step:

  1. Initial Submission: The Author creates an account and uploads their document, abstract, and related metadata.
  2. Quality Check & Payment Verification: The Editor receives the submission, ensures it meets basic formatting standards, and confirms that any required publication fees have been paid.
  3. The Peer-Review Phase: The Editor assigns one or more Reviewers to the manuscript. These Reviewers read the document and provide their expert feedback.
  4. The Editorial Decision: The Editor reviews the feedback collected from the Reviewers and makes an official decision. The manuscript can be officially accepted, outright rejected, or sent back to the author for changes.
  5. The Revision Loop (If Needed): If the document requires changes, the Author receives a notification. They must upload a corrected version along with a document explaining how they addressed the feedback. The Editor can then initiate a "Re-review," starting a fresh round of evaluations with the Reviewers.
  6. Final Publication: Once a manuscript is officially marked as "Accepted," an Administrator organizes it into a specific journal Volume and Issue, and finally clicks the "Publish" button to make it available to the public.

Proceed to Part 2: Guide for Authors for detailed instructions on submitting and managing research.

2. Guide for Authors

The Author portal provides a streamlined environment for researchers to submit their manuscripts, track the status of those submissions, and communicate with the editorial team through the revision process.

1. Registering and Logging In

Before any documents can be submitted, an account must be created on the platform.

  1. Navigate to the journal's homepage and locate the Register link, typically found in the top navigation menu.
  2. Fill out the registration form with accurate personal and professional details.
  3. Providing an ORCID iD: During registration, users are required to provide a valid ORCID iD (formatted as XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX). ORCID is a universal identifier that ensures your research is correctly attributed to you across different systems globally. If you do not have one, you can easily obtain it for free at the official ORCID website.

Once the account is created, use the Login page to access the Author Dashboard.

2. Submitting a New Manuscript

The dashboard serves as the central hub for all author activities. To begin a new submission:

  1. Locate and click the large button labeled "+ New Submission" near the top of the dashboard.
  2. Fill out the Details: You will be presented with a form. Carefully enter the manuscript's Title, a comprehensive Abstract, and relevant Keywords. These details help Editors understand your work at a glance.
  3. Upload Files: Use the file attachment section to upload your primary manuscript document. Ensure it is in an acceptable format (such as a PDF or Microsoft Word document).
  4. After verifying that all information is correct, click the Submit button at the bottom of the page.

Upon successful submission, the manuscript will appear on the dashboard with the status "Submitted". At this stage, the editorial team is notified to perform an initial review, verify any required submission payments, and assign peer reviewers.

3. Tracking Your Submission's Progress

Authors can check the status of their manuscripts at any time without needing to contact the editorial team.

The main dashboard lists all current and past submissions. Each submission displays a clear status badge indicating its current stage in the process.

By clicking on the title of any manuscript, users are taken to a detailed Submission Details page. This page provides a deeper look into the manuscript's history. Once the review process is underway, this page will update to reflect editorial decisions and display feedback.

4. Understanding and Submitting Revisions

Often, an Editor will decide that a manuscript has strong potential but requires modifications before it can be published. When this happens, the manuscript's status changes to "Needs Revision", and an email notification is sent out.

To submit the requested revisions:

  1. Log into the dashboard and click on the manuscript marked as "Needs Revision".
  2. Scroll down the page to find the Review History section. Here, you will be able to read the Public Comments left by the peer reviewers. It is highly recommended to read these carefully and use them to guide your corrections.
  3. Once the document has been corrected offline, locate and click the "Submit Revision" button on the manuscript page.
  4. Upload the New File: Attach the updated, corrected version of the manuscript.
  5. Response to Reviewers: A large text box is provided on this form. This is a crucial step. Use this space to clearly explain to the Editor and Reviewers exactly what changes were made in response to their feedback. If a suggested change was not made, politely explain why.
  6. Click the Submit button to finalize the revision.

Once the revision is submitted, the manuscript's status updates to "Revision Submitted". The Editor will be automatically alerted that the new version is ready, and they may choose to initiate a second round of peer review based on the submitted corrections.

3. Guide for Reviewers

Peer reviewers play a critical role in maintaining the academic integrity and quality of the journal. The reviewer interface is designed to make managing assignments and submitting feedback as straightforward as possible.

1. Handling Review Invitations

When an Editor identifies a user as a suitable reviewer for a specific manuscript, the system generates an email invitation.

To respond to an invitation: 1. Log into the system and navigate to the Reviewer Dashboard. 2. Look for the section labeled "Review Invitations". Here, the title and abstract of the proposed manuscript will be displayed to help inform the decision. 3. The user must choose to either Accept or Decline the invitation using the provided buttons. - Declining: If the user clicks Decline, a small prompt will appear asking for a brief reason (for example, "Conflict of interest" or "Currently unavailable due to workload"). Once submitted, the Editor is notified so they can find an alternative reviewer. - Accepting: If the user clicks Accept, the manuscript is immediately moved to the "Active Assignments" list. Full access to download and read the complete document is granted at this point.

2. Reading and Submitting an Assessment

Once an invitation is accepted, the reviewer is expected to read the document and provide a structured assessment.

  1. Locate the manuscript in the "Active Assignments" list on the dashboard and click its title to open the details page.
  2. Download the attached manuscript file to read offline.
  3. When ready to provide feedback, click the "Submit Review" button located on the page.
  4. The review form is split into three main sections:
  5. Recommendation: A dropdown menu requiring an official stance on the manuscript (e.g., Accept, Reject, Minor Revisions, Major Revisions). This helps the Editor gauge overall sentiment.
  6. Comments to Author: A text area for constructive, detailed feedback. Important: The text entered here will be visible to the Author once the Editor makes a decision. It should remain professional and objective.
  7. Confidential Comments to Editor: A secondary text area for private advice. The Author will never see this text. It is useful for flagging ethical concerns or providing blunt assessments directly to the editorial team.
  8. After completing the form, click Submit.

Upon submission, the assignment is marked as "Completed" on the dashboard. The Editor will automatically be notified once all assigned reviewers have submitted their respective assessments.

3. Navigating Re-reviews (Multiple Rounds)

The peer-review process often requires multiple rounds of evaluation. If an Editor asks an Author to make corrections based on initial feedback, the Author will eventually submit a revised document.

When this happens, the Editor may invite the original reviewers back to assess the changes. This is known as a Re-review (or Round 2, Round 3, etc.).

  • If invited for a Re-review, a new notification and invitation will appear on the dashboard.
  • Upon accepting the Re-review, the reviewer will notice a new section on the manuscript details page containing the Author's Response. This text explains exactly how the author addressed the previous criticisms, making it easier to evaluate the new version.
  • The reviewer can then click "Submit Review" to provide a fresh assessment for this new Round.

[!TIP] Viewing Past History: Reviewers can easily reference their past assessments. By scrolling down to the "Review History" section on a manuscript's detail page, older rounds of review can be viewed. Note that past rounds are permanently locked and are provided strictly for read-only reference.

4. Guide for Editors

Editors serve as the operational core of the publication process. They are responsible for managing incoming submissions, selecting appropriate peer reviewers, interpreting assessments, and making the final decisions on whether a manuscript is fit for publication.

1. Navigating the Editor Dashboard

The Editor Dashboard is designed to provide a comprehensive, high-level overview of the journal's current state.

  • Top Metrics: At the very top of the dashboard, highlight cards display key statistics, such as "Total Submissions" and the number of manuscripts that are currently "Unassigned" to any reviewers.
  • The Manuscripts Table: The main section of the dashboard is a large data table listing all manuscripts in the system.
  • Filtering: Dropdown menus at the top of the table allow the list to be filtered by Status (e.g., showing only manuscripts that are "Submitted", "Under Review", or "Accepted"). This is vital for managing large volumes of submissions.
  • Quick Actions: The far-right column of the table provides quick action buttons (like "Assign" or "Decide") to jump straight into tasks without needing to click through multiple pages.

2. Processing New Submissions and Payments

When a new manuscript enters the system, its status is marked as "Submitted". It is the Editor's responsibility to perform an initial screening.

  1. Click on the manuscript's title within the dashboard table to open its detailed view.
  2. Read the provided abstract and download the attached manuscript file. Ensure the document meets the journal's basic formatting guidelines and scope before advancing it to peer review.
  3. Verifying Payments: If the journal enforces a submission fee, look for the "Payment" column on the dashboard or the payment badge on the details page. If the author has paid via an external method (such as a bank transfer), the Editor must manually click the "Mark Paid" button to confirm receipt in the system.

3. Assigning Reviewers to a Manuscript

Once a manuscript passes the initial screening, peer reviewers must be selected.

  1. On the manuscript details page, scroll down to the "Assigned Reviewers" section.
  2. Click the "+ Assign Reviewer" button located at the bottom of the card. A modal window will appear.
  3. Use the dropdown list to select a registered user to act as a reviewer.
  4. The "Invite Only" Toggle: This is a crucial setting located below the dropdown.
  5. If checked (Recommended): The selected user will receive an email invitation. They will not be officially assigned until they manually click "Accept" on their dashboard.
  6. If unchecked: The selected user is forcibly assigned to the manuscript immediately, skipping the invitation phase. Use this only if prior verbal or email agreement has already been established.
  7. Click Assign to finalize the selection.

Tracking Reviewer Status

Once reviewers are selected, their progress can be monitored directly from the "Assigned Reviewers" card. Each reviewer will display a color-coded status badge: - Invited (Yellow): The invitation has been sent, but the user has not yet responded. - Declined (Red): The user actively rejected the invitation. The reason they provided will be displayed directly beneath their name, indicating that a replacement reviewer needs to be found. - Pending (Gray): The user accepted the invitation but has not yet submitted their assessment form. - Completed (Green): The user has successfully submitted their review.

4. Making Official Editorial Decisions

When all assigned reviewers have achieved a "Completed" status, it is time for the Editor to render a verdict.

  1. Review the submitted assessments. On the manuscript details page, both the "Public Comments" (intended for the author) and the "Confidential Advice" (intended only for the Editor) will be visible.
  2. Once a consensus is reached, click the large, prominent "Make Decision" button located near the top of the page.
  3. A form will appear requiring an official status update. Select one of the following from the dropdown:
  4. Accepted: The manuscript requires no further changes and is ready to be queued for publication.
  5. Rejected: The manuscript does not meet the journal's standards and the process is terminated.
  6. Needs Revision: The manuscript shows promise but the author must make corrections based on the provided feedback before a final decision can be made.
  7. Click Submit Decision. The Author will be automatically notified of this status change.

[!NOTE] Changing a Decision: The "Make Decision" button does not disappear after a verdict is rendered. Editors retain the ability to click it again to revoke an acceptance, or change a status at any point before the manuscript is officially published.

5. Publishing Articles to the Live Website

Once a manuscript has been officially Accepted and organized into an Issue, the Editor can release it to the public.

  1. Open the main Editor Dashboard and locate the target manuscript.
  2. Ensure the dashboard is showing accepted manuscripts (you can use the status filter).
  3. Look at the far-right column labeled "Actions."
  4. For manuscripts that meet all criteria, a distinct green "Publish" button will appear.
  5. Click this "Publish" button.
  6. The system will immediately change the manuscript's status to "Published". At this exact moment, the article becomes live and accessible on the public-facing website for the global community to read.

5. Handling Revisions and Requesting Re-reviews

If the Editor selected the "Needs Revision" status, the ball is placed in the Author's court. The system will pause until the Author submits their corrected document.

Once the Author completes this task, the manuscript's status updates to "Revision Submitted", and the Editor is alerted.

  1. Navigate back to the manuscript's detailed view.
  2. The newly uploaded file will be available for download. Crucially, the Author's "Response to Reviewers"—a text block explaining their corrections—will also be visible.
  3. Evaluating the Revisions:
  4. If the requested changes were minor (e.g., typos or formatting), the Editor may choose to simply click "Make Decision" and Accept the manuscript without further peer review.
  5. If the changes were major, the Editor should seek the reviewers' opinions again.
  6. Initiating a Re-review: Next to the name of any previous reviewer, click the "Request Re-review" button.
  7. This action automatically initiates Round 2 (or Round 3, etc.), sending a fresh invitation to that specific reviewer to assess the revised document against the author's stated responses.

The system meticulously tracks the history of these rounds. By scrolling down the manuscript page, Editors can review the separated historical data for "Round 1", "Round 2", ensuring no context is ever lost during lengthy revision cycles.

5. Guide for Administrators (Superadmins)

Administrators (often referred to as Superadmins or System Owners) possess the highest tier of access within the Journal Management System. They manage the core backend settings, user roles, and database tables through the highly secure Django Admin Interface.

Access the backend by appending /admin to your journal's URL (e.g., https://jhst.org/admin).

1. Managing Volumes and Issues

In academic publishing, accepted manuscripts are organized into specific "Issues" residing within a "Volume." Administrators control this packaging process from the backend.

  1. Accessing Volumes:
  2. On the Django Admin dashboard, scroll down to the Journal section and click on Volumes.

  3. Here, you can add a new Volume (typically representing the publication year) and manage existing ones.

  4. Accessing Issues:

  5. Under the Journal section, click on Issues.
  6. You can create a new Issue inside any existing Volume and assign specific publication dates to them.

2. Managing the Internal Team

While Authors and Reviewers can register their own accounts via the public website, internal staff roles—specifically Editors and Administrators—cannot be self-registered for security reasons. Administrators are exclusively responsible for provisioning and managing these privileged accounts.

  • Accessing Users:
  • On the Django Admin dashboard, locate the Authentication and Authorization section (or the Users section depending on your configuration) and click on Users.
  • Granting Permissions:
  • To elevate an existing user (such as a Reviewer who is being promoted to the editorial board), click on their username to open their profile.
  • Scroll down to the Permissions section.
  • Check the specific permission boxes—such as "Is editor", "Is reviewer", or "Superuser status" (for admin rights)—and click "Save".
  • The next time that user logs in, the system will recognize their new authority and grant them access to the appropriate dashboards and tools.

End of Journal System User Manual.
